articles.title: Sixty Countries. Four Hundred Athletes. India Just Turned Yoga Into a Competitive Sport With an Olympic Ambition.
articles.excerpt: The first World Yogasana Championship opened in Ahmedabad on Thursday, with electronic scoring, six age categories, and a clear pitch for Olympic recognition.
articles.image_caption: Athletes performing yogasana during a competitive event
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora in the US, UK, and Canada — where yoga studios outnumber cricket clubs — the World Yogasana Championship reframes a cultural practice they have long practiced recreationally as an internationally competitive sport with Olympic aspirations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two World No. 1 Rankings. Seventeen Top-10 Finishes Across Twenty Weight Classes. Indian Boxing Has Never Been This Deep.
articles.excerpt: Minakshi Hooda and Jaismine Lamboria both hold the top spot in their divisions. India now features in the top 10 of nine of ten women's and eight of ten men's weight categories.
articles.image_caption: Jaismine Lamboria during an international boxing competition
articles.nri_angle: For NRI fans tracking India's Olympic medal prospects, the rankings signal unprecedented depth across weight classes. With Asian Games seedings in Aichi-Nagoya determined by these standings, Indian boxers enter with two No. 1 seeds and multiple top-three placements.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Beat Carlsen With White. Then He Beat Carlsen With Black. Praggnanandhaa Is Half a Point Behind the Leader With One Round to Go.
articles.excerpt: Only Viswanathan Anand had done it before. The 20-year-old from Chennai now has two classical wins over the world's number one in the same tournament at Norway Chess 2026.
articles.image_caption: R Praggnanandhaa, the 20-year-old Indian grandmaster competing at Norway Chess 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indian chess is in a golden era — Praggnanandhaa becomes only the second Indian after Anand to beat Carlsen twice in one event, while the world champion Gukesh and women's players Divya Deshmukh and Koneru Humpy also compete at Norway Chess.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: They Were Born in Auckland, Doha, Melbourne, and Paris. All Four Trace Their Roots to India. All Four Are Going to the World Cup.
articles.excerpt: Sarpreet Singh, Tahsin Mohammed, Nishan Velupillay, and Samuel Moutoussamy will represent four different nations at the 2026 FIFA World Cup — the largest group of Indian-origin players at a single tournament in history.
articles.image_caption: Sarpreet Singh during training with FC Bayern Munich in 2019
articles.nri_angle: Four players of Indian origin — from Punjab, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Indo-Guadeloupean Tamil roots — represent New Zealand, Qatar, Australia, and DR Congo at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the largest Indian-heritage presence at the tournament since Vikash Dhorasoo in 2006.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'In a Family of Four, We All Lived the Same Dream.' KS Bharat Retires From International Cricket at 32.
articles.excerpt: The Visakhapatnam wicketkeeper-batter played seven Tests for India, including the 2023 WTC final at The Oval, before stepping away with an emotional note thanking Kohli, Rohit, and Dravid.
articles.image_caption: A wicketkeeper in action during a cricket test match
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satwik and Chirag Were Out. Hariharan and Arjun Stepped In. India Has a Second Doubles Pair at the Super 1000 Level.
articles.excerpt: MR Arjun and Hariharan Amsakarunan fought back from a game down to reach the Indonesia Open quarterfinals — a first for any Indian men's doubles pair outside the Satwik-Chirag partnership at a BWF Super 1000 event.
articles.image_caption: Badminton doubles players in action during a professional tournament
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rights Groups Say NRI Fans Face a 'Climate of Fear' at the World Cup. FIFA Has Not Responded.
articles.excerpt: With the tournament kicking off June 11 across the United States, the Sport and Rights Alliance warns that Trump's immigration crackdown has turned the world's biggest sporting event into a source of anxiety for diaspora fans and travellers on temporary visas.
articles.image_caption: Football fans celebrate in the stands during a major international tournament
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pant Lost the Vice-Captaincy and the LSG Armband. His Coaches Say the Problem Is Not Leadership. It Is Shot Selection.
articles.excerpt: Ryan ten Doeschate and childhood coach Devender Sharma say India's wicketkeeper must stop forcing horizontal shots and start playing to the match situation. The Afghanistan Test is his proving ground.
articles.image_caption: A cricket wicketkeeper-batter in action during a match
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sindhu Lost to An Se Young Again. Ayush Shetty Fell After Winning the First Game. India's Singles Campaign at the Indonesia Open Is Over.
articles.excerpt: Six Indian singles players entered the draw. All six are out by the second round. Only the doubles pairs remain in Jakarta.
articles.image_caption: PV Sindhu, double Olympic medallist, at a public event
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thirty Goals Scored, Two Conceded. India's U-18 Hockey Teams Are Dismantling the Asia Cup.
articles.excerpt: The women beat Singapore 25-0. The men hammered Chinese Taipei 13-1. Both teams are in the semifinals in Kakamigahara, Japan.
articles.image_caption: India women's hockey in action at the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kohli Is Out. He Played Through the Hamstring Strain in the Final. Now He Will Miss the Entire Afghanistan ODI Series.
articles.excerpt: Ruturaj Gaikwad replaces Kohli in the ODI squad. Rajat Patidar is in line for India A. The BCCI has advised at least two weeks of rest.
articles.image_caption: Virat Kohli at an official event in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sony Will Broadcast the Sri Lanka Tri-Series Live. They Are Doing It Because a Fifteen-Year-Old Is in the Squad.
articles.excerpt: A-team cricket does not get televised. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's inclusion in the India A squad for the Dambulla tri-series changed that overnight.
articles.image_caption: The India A tri-series in Dambulla will be broadcast live on Sony Sports, driven by Sooryavanshi's star power
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ashwin Has His Eyes on Dubey. Kumble Wants Kuldeep. The Afghanistan Test Has a Spin Selection Puzzle Nobody Agrees On.
articles.excerpt: With four spinners in a fifteen-man squad, India's greatest modern spinner says the uncapped left-armer from Vidarbha is the one he wants to see bowl first.
articles.image_caption: R. Ashwin, India's all-time leading off-spinner, has backed Harsh Dubey for a Test debut
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Beat Bangladesh 3-0 in the Group Stage. They Meet Again on Friday in Goa. This Time, the Trophy Is on the Line.
articles.excerpt: The Blue Tigresses face defending champions Bangladesh in the SAFF Women's Championship final on June 6 in Margao, seeking their sixth title at home after a semifinal scare against Bhutan.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sooryavanshi, Tilak, and Gaikwad Board the Plane to Dambulla. India A's Tri-Series Is the World Cup Audition Nobody Is Calling an Audition.
articles.excerpt: A 15-player squad led by Tilak Varma leaves for Sri Lanka next week for a seven-match ODI tri-series against Sri Lanka A and Afghanistan A — and at least half the names on the list are playing for a senior spot in 2027.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Lost the First Game 8-21. Forty Minutes Later, Ayush Shetty Was the Last Indian Man Standing in Jakarta.
articles.excerpt: The 20-year-old from Mangaluru rallied from a one-sided opening loss to stun China's world No. 15, keeping India's men's singles hopes alive at the Indonesia Open after Lakshya, Srikanth, and Prannoy all exited early.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Won the World Championship Seven Months Ago. At Norway Chess, Gukesh Is in Last Place.
articles.excerpt: Three classical defeats, a 25-point rating slide, and a drop to world number 22. The youngest world champion in history is learning what the title costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ten Days Before Kickoff, India Finally Has a World Cup Broadcaster. Here Is What It Means for NRI Fans.
articles.excerpt: Zee Entertainment's last-minute $60 million deal secures FIFA rights through 2034. For diaspora viewers in the US, UK, and Canada, Zee5 streaming is the answer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ten Gold Medals. Nineteen Total. India's U20 Athletes Just Had Their Best Overseas Championship in History.
articles.excerpt: At the Asian U20 Athletics Championships in Hong Kong, a squad of teenage Indians broke records, outpaced Japan, and qualified for the World Championships in Eugene, Oregon.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: She Has Lost Nine Straight Matches Against An Se Young. On Wednesday in Jakarta, Sindhu Will Try Again.
articles.excerpt: PV Sindhu's Indonesia Open run — and her return to the world's top 10 — now runs directly through the most dominant player in women's badminton.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Won the T20 World Cup Three Months Ago. Now Suryakumar Yadav Is About to Lose the Captaincy.
articles.excerpt: The BCCI has decided to move on from SKY as T20I captain. Shreyas Iyer, Ishan Kishan, and Tilak Varma are in the race to replace him ahead of the Ireland series.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nongrum Scored in the 58th Minute. India Beat Bhutan 1-0. The Blue Tigresses Are in the SAFF Final.
articles.excerpt: After scoring 14 goals in the group stage, India needed just one against a resolute Bhutan in the semifinal. Bangladesh await in Thursday's final at Margao.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: They Won the Singapore Open Six Days Ago. On Wednesday in Jakarta, Satwik Pointed to His Shoulder and Walked Off.
articles.excerpt: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy's recurring right shoulder injury forced India's top doubles pair to retire from the Indonesia Open first round. The BAI says recovery is now the priority.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rohit and Kohli Will Be at Mullanpur on June 9. The Afghanistan Test Will Still Be Going. The BCCI Is Running Both.
articles.excerpt: India's ODI squad will hold a three-day preparatory camp at the same ground where the one-off Test against Afghanistan may still be in progress. The staff will split. The net bowlers are already drafted. The temperature is forty degrees.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sindhu Won. Lakshya Lost. Srikanth Lost. India's Indonesia Open Started With One Player Carrying the Entire Country.
articles.excerpt: PV Sindhu, back in the world top ten after 954 days, beat Busanan Ongbamrungphan for a 21st time. Lakshya Sen and Kidambi Srikanth both fell in the opening round of the Super 1000 event in Jakarta.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wesley So Leads Norway Chess With Two Rounds Left. Praggnanandhaa Is Two Points Behind. Carlsen Is Fifth.
articles.excerpt: Round eight produced two classical decisive games — Praggnanandhaa beat Carlsen for the second time, Firouzja defeated Gukesh — and the standings heading into the final stretch look nothing like the pre-tournament predictions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pat Cummins Says Something Has to Give in 2027. It Will Not Be Test Cricket. That Leaves the IPL.
articles.excerpt: Australia's captain has signalled he may skip the IPL entirely next year, prioritising four Tests in India, a 150th anniversary Ashes match, a full Ashes tour, and the ODI World Cup over a $1.9 million SRH contract.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIM Indore Will Study the 'Vaibhav Model.' A Fifteen-Year-Old Cricketer Is Now a Management Case Study.
articles.excerpt: The institute's multidisciplinary research will examine how early fame, family support, and mental resilience shaped Sooryavanshi's record-breaking IPL 2026 season — and what it means for identifying talent beyond cricket.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pandya Is in Bengaluru. Rohit Is Not. India's Two Biggest ODI Stars Must Pass Fitness Tests Before They Can Play Afghanistan.
articles.excerpt: Hardik Pandya has reported to the BCCI Centre of Excellence for a week of drills and match simulations. Rohit Sharma was told to do the same. There is no update on when he will arrive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The BCCI Has Named Sairaj Bahutule as India's Spin Bowling Coach. He Replaces a Vacancy No One Wanted to Talk About.
articles.excerpt: The 53-year-old domestic legend with 630 first-class wickets joins Gambhir's staff ahead of the Afghanistan series. His brief: rebuild India's spin identity after Ashwin's retirement and Jadeja's absence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Twelve Matches. Five Cities. Two Tests. India's New Zealand Tour Will Be the Biggest in NZC History.
articles.excerpt: New Zealand Cricket has unveiled a 42-day, all-format itinerary starting in October. For NRIs in Australasia, it is the home-summer event of a lifetime.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: She Won in the Supreme Court. She Won on the Scales. On the Mat, Vinesh Phogat Lost the Only Bout That Mattered.
articles.excerpt: After months of legal battles, a maternity return, and a last-minute weight class reprieve, the three-time Olympian's Asian Games bid ended with a 4-6 semifinal defeat to Meenakshi Goyat at the Indira Gandhi Stadium.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: No Gill. No Suryakumar. Sooryavanshi Is In. The BCCI's Asian Games Longlist Is a Statement About What Comes Next.
articles.excerpt: India's 30-man preliminary squad for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games drops both white-ball captains and includes a 15-year-old. The government wants a full-strength team. The selectors have other plans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kumble Wants Kuldeep. Pathan Wants Washington. India's Test XI for Afghanistan Has Two Spots Still in Play.
articles.excerpt: The one-off Test at Mullanpur starts June 6. Gill will captain for the first time. The bowling combination remains the only question.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Four Classical Losses in Eight Rounds. Magnus Carlsen Is Second-to-Last at Norway Chess. Praggnanandhaa Has Beaten Him Twice.
articles.excerpt: The five-time world champion has nine points with two rounds left. Wesley So leads with fourteen. Carlsen's worst classical run in years has turned Oslo into someone else's tournament.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gulveer Singh Ran a 3:55 Mile. He Is the First Indian to Break the Four-Minute Barrier. He Did It in Cleveland.
articles.excerpt: The army runner's historic performance capped a week in which Indian athletes shattered barriers across the 100m, 400m, mile, high jump, and decathlon — all within days of each other.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Four Players of Indian Heritage Will Take the Field at the FIFA World Cup. None of Them Play for India.
articles.excerpt: From Punjab to Auckland, Kerala to Doha, and Tamil Nadu to Melbourne — the diaspora will be represented at football's grandest stage even as the Blue Tigers watch from home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Assaubayeva Beat Divya Deshmukh in the Decisive Round. The Norway Chess Women's Title Is All but Settled.
articles.excerpt: The Kazakh star leads by 5.5 points with two rounds left. Divya drops to joint third. Humpy finishes last among six.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rohit and Kohli Are Back. Ishan Kishan Returns After Three Years. India's ODI Squad for Afghanistan Is a Statement.
articles.excerpt: Hardik Pandya's inclusion is subject to fitness clearance. Prince Yadav earns a maiden call-up. The three-match series starts June 13 in Dharamsala.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harmanpreet Made 56 Not Out. Capsey Made 45 Off 21 Balls. England Chased Down 180 to Win the Final T20I at Taunton.
articles.excerpt: India posted their highest score of the series but England's Alice Capsey dismantled the target in 18.3 overs, raising concerns about India's T20 World Cup preparation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Has Now Beaten Carlsen Twice in Classical. Praggnanandhaa's Norway Chess Resurgence Is the Story of the Tournament.
articles.excerpt: The Indian grandmaster defeated the world number one in Round 8, while Firouzja beat Gukesh to tighten the title race heading into the final two rounds in Oslo.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ten Wrestlers Entered. Ten Won Medals. India's Women Swept the U17 Asian Championships Without Dropping a Single Athlete.
articles.excerpt: At the U17 Asian Wrestling Championships in Da Nang, India achieved a 100 per cent podium finish with two gold, three silver, and five bronze. Days earlier, the U23 men's freestyle team won the championship outright.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: They Lost Four Straight Finals in Two Years. In Singapore, Satwik and Chirag Finally Won — and Made History.
articles.excerpt: The Indian pair became the first to win the Singapore Open doubles title, ending a two-year drought by beating the world No. 1 and No. 3 pairs back to back. Now they lead India's charge at the Indonesia Open.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Hundred and Fifty Players. No Contracts. The ISL's Off-Season Has Become an Existential Crisis.
articles.excerpt: As 150 Indian Super League players enter free agency without new deals, a commercial rights dispute between clubs and the AIFF has left Indian football's top division in limbo — and families across the northeast are feeling it first.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Was Written Off at Thirty-Four. At Thirty-Six, He Took More Wickets Than Any Indian Pacer in a Single IPL Season.
articles.excerpt: Bhuvneshwar Kumar's reinvention at RCB — wobbly seam, relentless discipline, and 28 wickets — has forced India's selectors into a debate they thought was settled four years ago.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zero Goals. Two Defeats. India's Blue Tigers Left London Without Scoring. Now They Head to Tajikistan.
articles.excerpt: India's Unity Cup campaign ended in embarrassment — no goals in two matches — and Khalid Jamil's squad now faces two friendlies in Tajikistan with star forward Ryan Williams ruled out.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Took 104 Wickets in Two Ranji Seasons. He Won Player of the Tournament. The BCCI Called Him — as a Backup.
articles.excerpt: Auqib Nabi, the 24-year-old pace spearhead who led Jammu & Kashmir to their first Ranji Trophy title, has been named as a backup player for India's Test against Afghanistan. Not in the squad. Not as a reserve. As a standby.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pant Has Lost the Test Vice-Captaincy. He Has Been Dropped from ODIs. The Selectors Say They Still Rate Him.
articles.excerpt: KL Rahul replaces Rishabh Pant as Shubman Gill's deputy for the Afghanistan Test. The BCCI says the move is about helping Pant become 'the best Test player he has always been.' The ODI squad tells a different story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Test. Six ODIs. Seven T20Is. Two Tours. India's Next Sixty Days Are the Most Crowded in Cricket History.
articles.excerpt: From Mullanpur to Chennai to Belfast to Lord's, India's post-IPL schedule is a marathon. Here is what every NRI cricket fan needs to know.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Four Days. Sixteen IPL Matches. One Test as Captain. Shubman Gill Faces the Hardest Transition in Indian Cricket.
articles.excerpt: India's players go straight from the IPL final to a one-off Test against Afghanistan at a venue that has never hosted Test cricket. The workload crisis is real.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
